item.title: Iran claims another attack targeting U.S. radar site in Bahrain
item.description: Iran has claimed to hit U.S. radar systems in Bahrain three times in less than a week, but authorities said the first two attacks were intercepted.

item.title: This teen had no place to go, so a hospital became his home
item.description: A young survivor of gun violence lived on the third floor of a St. Louis children's hospital, moving through the halls in a wheelchair, on and off for over three years. He said it became his home when he had nowhere safe to go.

item.title: Trump in Asia for Putin, Xi summit; possible Kim meeting
item.description: The president arrived in Manila for the start of a multi-day swing in Asia, where he's scheduled to meet with Russia's Vladimir Putin and China's Xi Jinping in a highly anticipated summit. He says he may also meet with North Korea's Kim Jong Un.

item.title: Widespread service outages at major U.S. banks appear to be over
item.description: Customers at JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and other major financial institutions reported difficulty accessing their accounts.

item.title: Experts and reporters break down FAA meltdown, explaining what's responsible
item.description: Before the Federal Aviation Administration air travel meltdown on Friday, transportation officials had received years of warnings, records show. CBS News examines what Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says is the likely origin of the outage and how the Trump administration is responding.

item.title: Protests flare in Philippines over Trump's visit and planned AI hub
item.description: Protests against President Trump's visit to the Philippines have popped up around the country, as local residents criticize a Trump administration project to build an artificial intelligence hub.

item.title: 3 killed when minivan crashes into Los Angeles food stand
item.description: At least three people were killed, and two others were severely injured when a minivan crashed into a food stand near a Metro bus stop in North Hollywood.

item.title: Can We Still Trust American Air Travel?
item.description: The FAA grounded every departing flight in the U.S. on Friday, only the second nationwide ground stop since 9/11. CBS News senior transportation correspondent Kris Van Cleave on why anyone would swap out equipment at 4 p.m. on a Friday, what doesn't add up in the official story, and why he's still flying. If you'd like to share your own great question, email us at greatquestion@cbsnews.com.

item.title: Kyiv under attack from Russian ballistic missiles after Ukraine's overnight attack on Russia
item.description: Even as Jared Kushner says progress is being made to end the war between Russia and Ukraine, the two nations continue to launch attacks against each other. CBS News international reporter Aidan Stretch reports on the latest in the fighting.

item.title: Democrat Mary Peltola leads ongoing Alaska Senate race
item.description: Nearly two weeks after the midterms, the only Senate race that hasn't been called is in Alaska. CBS News' Anthony Salvanto has the latest.

item.title: Explaining the FAA's modernization efforts amid Friday's nationwide ground stop
item.description: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said this weekend that 70% of FAA telecommunication network's copper wires have been replaced with fiber-optic cables, but the process only began last year when the cables were already more than 60 years old. "The Daily Report" explains, and CBS News investigative reporter Josh Boswell reports on warnings of technical failures.

item.title: Raye and Rosalía lead 2027 Grammy nominations
item.description: The Grammy nominations were announced on Monday, and Raye led the charge with 11 nods. She's up for record and song of the year for "Where Is My Husband" and album of the year for "This Music May Contain Hope." Entertainment Tonight correspondent Denny Directo breaks down the nominations and discusses Robert Pattinson landing the role of James Bond.

item.title: United Airlines says it resolved a system outage
item.description: A memo from the union representing United Airlines pilots indicated the issue was with the airline's weight and balance calculation system.

item.title: Boy with autism works to help other kids like himself, landing him Time's "Kid of the Year"
item.description: Nine-year-old Ledger Mann took the initiative to create comfort bags for police to use when searching for lost kids who may have autism or sensory challenges, like himself. Time magazine recognized his efforts and named him "Kid of the Year." Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Bodycam video shows police breaking up massive Virginia house party
item.description: A husband and wife in Virginia are facing charges over a wild house party for their teenagers that police say involved underage drinking and fireworks. The couple said it was crashed by hundreds of teens. Jericka Duncan has the body camera footage.

item.title: Top federal prosecutor in Houston accused of breaking ethics rules
item.description: A nonprofit watchdog group filed an ethics complaint on Monday against the top federal prosecutor in Houston, alleging he has violated professional conduct rules by threatening to prosecute Democratic lawmakers.

item.title: New James Bond is announced after rampant speculation
item.description: After rampant online speculation about who would take over the iconic spy character from Daniel Craig, the franchise announced who the new 007 will be.

item.title: Robert Pattinson lands coveted James Bond role
item.description: Going back more than 60 years, only six actors have played James Bond, the British secret agent code-named 007. After years of speculation, Amazon MGM Studios cast 40-year-old Robert Pattinson as the leading man. Tom Hanson has the story.

item.title: U.S. loses measles elimination status as cases surge nationwide
item.description: The United States has lost its official measles elimination status for the first time in 26 years. Here's what to know.

item.title: Pacific Coast sees monster waves, a dread for some, but a delight for the surfers
item.description: Some of the biggest waves in years continued to hit the Pacific Coast shoreline on Monday. Carter Evans takes a look at the monster waves.

item.title: Doctor says U.S. losing measles elimination status is a "huge public health failure"
item.description: The United States is expected to officially lose its status as a country that has eliminated measles after reporting the highest case total in more than 30 years. CBS News chief medical correspondent Dr. Jon LaPook puts it into perspective.

item.title: 2 self-driving Waymos involved in 4-car collision in Phoenix
item.description: Police in Phoenix, Arizona, are investigating a four-vehicle crash that included two driverless Waymo vehicles. Three people were rushed to the hospital, including one who is fighting for their life. Jason Allen reports.

item.title: Trump traveling to China amid Nvidia scandal fallout
item.description: President Trump was on his way to Asia for a historic three-way meeting with the leaders of Russia and China. The meeting comes amid the fallout from the Nvidia scandal, but the president tried to downplay the impact. Weijia Jiang has more.

item.title: United Airlines resolved system outage that delayed many departures
item.description: A glitch at United Airlines delayed a full return to normal for an industry still recovering from a nationwide tech-related ground stop on Friday evening. Kris Van Cleave reports.

item.title: "Tiger team" formed to head off another nationwide ground stop
item.description: Members of the new tiger team include officials from the FAA, Office of the Director of National Intelligence, Defense Department and Transportation Department.

item.title: 11/16: CBS Evening News
item.description: Outages hit major U.S. banks, including Chase and Bank of America; United Airlines experienced a "widespread system outage."

item.title: 11/16: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: What we know about the cause of Friday's nationwide ground stop; Trump to meet with Putin and Xi during Asia trip.

item.title: Epstein's death may not have been suicide, new analysis suggests
item.description: Forensics expert Dr. Michael Freeman says multiple images and overlooked details about Jeffrey Epstein's death contradict the conclusion that he died by suicide.

item.title: Diesel prices dip below $6 a gallon for first time since September
item.description: Diesel around the U.S. now averages $5.99 a gallon, down from a record high of $6.53 in September, according to AAA.

item.title: Officials received years of warnings before FAA ground stop
item.description: For years, audits flagged billions of dollars thrown at non-competitive contracts beset with delays, amid repeated technology breakdowns.
